anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode (A2, pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode (K2, pin 2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT, so both ends of the LED sit on the same net. The LED has no potential across it and cannot light. The sibling channel D30 K1 returns through R59 to GND, which is the expected sink arrangement.
anomalies.expected: The K2 side of R60 should return to a reference such as GND, as K1 does through R59, so that D30 channel 2 is a working indicator of the e-stop output.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop status LED for channel 2 never lights, so the indicator gives no reliable e-stop state. The safety chain itself is not affected.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three LEDs D4, D14 and D23 are the only pins on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW. No supply, switch or driver component is connected to that net.
anomalies.expected: The net should be driven from a 3.3V source, directly or through a switch, so that the Ethernet and PI activity LEDs can be powered.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity LEDs and the PI activity LED have no anode supply and will stay dark, so the status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: The red LED D2 has its anode on the open-drain output U27.Y (pin 4). Its cathode goes through R31 to GND. Every other LED driven from an SN74LVC1G07 sink (D1, D12, D17, D8, D28, D29) has the anode on the supply side and the cathode on the buffer output. D2 is reversed relative to that scheme.
anomalies.expected: For an open-drain sink output, the LED anode should be on the supply side through a resistor, and the cathode should be on the buffer output, as in D1 and D12.
anomalies.impact: D2 cannot be sourced by the open-drain output, so this status indicator will not light.
